summary: Recommended design is Option P: reuse the existing precedent and fail closed. No source or test files were edited. Diagnostics show a native marker can reach lpad's repeated s/width positions only through a capturing-let read (scalar/exists/IN) whose inline body holds a bind-safe literal or a header parameter. Bind-safe literals are never call arguments (classify -> CALL_ARGUMENT), and header reads in lpad stay PIE-S2355. The candidate's family-specific walker repetition (rows._tree_nodes/_value_nodes family + (0,1,0,0,1,2), ast realize_rows/spliced_value_nodes/row_parameter_leaves family threading) has no observable effect: candidate as-is and candidate with that repetition removed gave identical output on every probed source, and every inline shape is BLOCKED PIE-B1008 either way. Removing it brings ast.py back to base. It also leaves one authored-node walker, so all consumers share one order (fixes R2) and no residual use is ever claimed (fixes R1). The canonical authority is: one realized native leaf <-> exactly one NativeUse <-> exactly one rendered parameter token. The leaf order is defined once by ast.row_parameter_leaves. The independent verifier (verify_row_bytes byte re-derivation + verify_row_parameters token/leaf/use equality) and the pure boundary (_Check claims, _Tokens order) compare that order against the token stream from the actual rendered bytes. Any leaf rendered twice therefore fails closed, and builder and verifier cannot share a blind spot about repeats. MySQL lpad then admits exactly what PostgreSQL lpad admits. PG output is byte-identical to base f8ccd2c4 (checked by running the same sources against an exported base tree). The design also found R3, a new candidate defect: the MySQL pure boundary rejects lpad with a literal Text first operand ('lpad realization', INVALID_RELATION). _value_realization has no image for a my_utf8mb4_text anchor, and the candidate replaced base _is_pg_text_value. Fix: restore the base PG predicate word for word and add a MySQL arm limited to lpad that also accepts an anchored my_utf8mb4_text literal. Also needed: correct the docs/release-note claim that the candidate 'preserves every repeated lpad occurrence', make mechanical format repairs, and rename the test that carries the slice name. The alternative, Option O (MySQL admits repeated markers), needs either per-occurrence inline-let realization, which breaks the single-read invariant, or leaf->uses multiplicity across the AST, observation schema, pure boundary, and compiled and binding verifiers. It would also put MySQL ahead of PG, so it is classified USER_DECISION_REQUIRED.
pg_current_behavior: PostgreSQL renders one SQLParameter/SQLParameterRead per authored operand and emits the same '$k' (server index from leaf.use) each time the renderer visits that operand. lpad visits s/width 3/2 times, round(Float) visits its operand 5 times, and starts_with/ends_with visit the second argument twice. The walkers (rendered_value_nodes/rendered_tree_nodes, row_parameter_leaves) visit each node once. verify_row_parameters requires len(parameter_uses) == len(leaves) == len(parameter tokens), so a native leaf inside a repeated operand produces extra tokens and the artifact is refused: BLOCKED [('PIE-B1008', 'fixed_value_or_parameter_correspondence')]. Measured on base f8ccd2c4: PG lpad with a capturing-let scalar read at width or text, with bind-safe 'x'/7 or header param lo in the let's WHERE, is BLOCKED with that blocker, and so is starts_with with the read at the second argument. In practice this path is reachable only through capturing-let inline bodies, because bind-safe literals are never call arguments and header reads in lpad are PIE-S2355. On direct shapes (bound literals in lets feeding lpad), PG is VERIFIED with each marker rendered once, and its SQL bytes are identical between base and candidate. MySQL starts_with/ends_with is an existing admitted construct with a repeated operand; it uses the same mechanism and is BLOCKED PIE-B1008 on both base and candidate.

risks: Option P does not provide R1's literal success witness for a repeated MySQL marker. Such shapes, reachable only through capturing-let reads, fail closed with PIE-B1008 as on PG and as with MySQL/PG starts_with. Reviewer/owner must accept the precedent; admitting them is Option O and USER_DECISION_REQUIRED, because MySQL would lead PG and break the single-read or leaf-use contracts.

The refusal surfaces as PIE-B1008 fixed_value_or_parameter_correspondence (an internal-correspondence detail), not a PIE-B1003 rule. This is existing PG behavior; making it an explicit builder refusal would change PG public blockers and needs separate authorization.

R3 is a newly found candidate defect outside R1/R2: the MySQL pure boundary rejects lpad with a literal Text first operand. If it is not fixed, W1's MySQL observation assertions fail. The fix must keep the base PG predicate (_is_pg_text_value/_is_pg_text_input) word for word and must not widen _value_realization for other MySQL checks.

The test-side probe.decode_public cannot decode any lpad document (PG included, from base onward: 'closed scalar call spelling') nor two-source VERIFIED capturing-let documents ('invalid public artifact'). The success witness relies on the pure boundary plus verify_emission_observation instead.
Two-source labelled witness sources with let chains fail compiled export with COMPILED_EXPORT_SOURCE_BINDING (PG on base too). This is an existing limitation; W1 uses the single-source fixture.

Candidate format damage (comment appended to the 'if name in {lpad, add_months}' line in rendering.py, misindented dict in verification.py ~7428, long lines) will fail ruff format --check until fixed mechanically.
Docs and release-note fragment currently claim every repeated lpad occurrence is preserved in placeholder order; both must be corrected to PG-parity wording.
MySQL native qualification (DB campaign) is still pending; nothing here is DB evidence.
